title.narrative: Higher Education for Technology and Innovation Project

description.narrative: The proposed project will support the government?s human capital development agenda by strengthening the capacity of two public universities?the Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember (ITS) in East Java Province and Universitas Lampung (UNILA) in Lampung Province?to provide cutting edge higher education and high-quality research?two key drivers of technology development and innovation. It will provide world-class academic facilities and innovation centers, and will strengthen faculty, staff, and student capacity to teach, research, and innovate. It will support the construction of a teaching hospital to boost capacity to develop high-quality health personnel and provide quality medical services to respond to increased demand for health services, including those triggered by the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic. The project will provide new research facilities and grants to stimulate commercialization of new products and foster collaboration between universities and industry.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Indicator Indicator: 250 research, innovation, and entrepreneurship grants provided to ITS academic staff (at least 32% of whom are female) in specialized areas Achievement: 265 Progress/Status: Achieved ITS has provided grants with a total amount of: - 2022: Rp 7.1 billion allocated to fund 48 activity topics (research, innovation, and entrepreneurship), involving 421 participants, of whom 40.62% were women. - 2023: Rp 15 billion allocated to fund 70 activity topics, involving 624 participants, of whom 44.39% were women. - 2024 (batch 1 & 2): Rp 16.9 billion allocated to fund 110 activity topics, involving 902 participants, of whom 46.01% were women. - 2025: Rp 4.2 billion allocated to fund 52 activity topics, involving 292 participants, of whom 56.16% were women.
Data Source: MOECRT annual progress reports and ITS annual monitoring reports

Output: Cutting edge education and research in priority sectors delivered by ITS Indicator: UNILA upgraded with a new and equipped pandemic-ready teaching hospital with gender-responsive, earthquake-resilient, and climate-smart features Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Ongoing Civil Works. The Civil Work (CWU) package consists of RSPTN, IRC, and WWTP. The contractor is PT. Nindya Karya. A total of 100 beds are available in RSPTN. Construction has been completed; the Provisional Handing Over (BAST#1) was issued on 24 April 2026, with a 365-day maintenance period until April 2027.
Equipment and Furniture. Procurement of 10 equipment and furniture packages has been tendered and is scheduled for contract award in Q3 2026.
Data Source: MOECRT annual progress reports and UNILA annual monitoring reports

Output: Indicator Indicator: 1,100 staff of UNILA Faculty of Medicine and other facultieso (at least 50% of whom are female) trained, resulting in increased knowledge and research skills in the life sciences, and hospital management capacity Achievement: 1,134 Progress/Status: Substantially Achieved - 2022: 122 staff trained (publication writing workshops, fellowship programs in biomolecular and flow cytometry labs); 59% female. - 2023: 717 staff trained (publication writing clinics, AI and patent drafting training, research-center and international-laboratory-based training, fellowship programs, international medical fellowships); 62.3% female. - 2024: 183 staff trained (research-center and international-laboratory-based training, advanced AI and statistical analysis training, fellowship programs, international/domestic medical fellowships); 68.8% female. - 2025: 112 staff trained (medical research training, fellowship programs); 79.4% female.
During 2022-2025, a total of 1,134 staff members of the UNILA Faculty of Medicine and other faculties (64.7% women) participated in training. Data Source: MOECRT annual progress reports and UNILA annual monitoring reports Actual value: 1,134

Output: Indicator Indicator: 395 ITS teaching and technical staff (at least 32% of whom are female)l trained, resulting in increased knowledge in specialized areas Achievement: 556 Progress/Status: Achieved By December 2025 (for the years 2022 to 2025), a total of 629 ITS teaching and technical staff were trained, with female participation of 40.06%. - 2022: 127 teaching staff and 247 technical staff (38.77% women) - 2023: 36 teaching staff and 18 technical staff (38.89% women) - 2024: 120 teaching staff and 9 technical staff (41.86% women) - 2025: 72 teaching staff (44.44% women).
Data Source: MOECRT annual progress reports and ITS annual monitoring reports

Output: Indicator Indicator: Five applied research programs in the health sector launched by UNILA Achievement: 5 Progress/Status: Achieved Applied research consists of five topics aligned with UNILA's IRC strengths: tropical medicine; biomolecular, genetic, and degenerative disease; pathology and toxicology; clinical trial and diagnostic trial laboratory; and food nutrition laboratory. These five topics have been further expanded into 10 research topics: infectious disease, tropical medicine, biomolecular and genetic, degenerative disease, pathology, clinical toxicology, clinical trial, diagnostic trial, food and nutrition, and nutrigenomic research. The UNILA HETI project research grant was implemented from 2022 to 2025, covering all applied research topics (batches 1 and 2 lasting 3 years, batch 3 lasting 2 years, batch 4 lasting 1 year, plus micro research). Details are in Appendix 10. Research publications in reputable international journals related to medicine and health at UNILA from 2022 to 2025 totaled 1,031. The total number of IPRs/Patents at UNILA from 2022 to 2025 is 1,342 (across medicine/health and other science, technology, and social science fields).
Data Source: MOECRT annual progress reports and UNILA annual monitoring reports

Output: Indicator Indicator: ITS upgraded with four new and equipped innovation centers, one academic building (with classrooms and laboratories), and one cultural and language center (all with gender-responsive, earthquake-resilient, and climate-smart features)gender responsive, earthquake-resilient, green, energy-efficient infrastructure) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Ongoing ITS has completed the construction of four new innovation centers, including the Maritime Center, Automotive Center, Creative Center, and ICT Robotics Center. In addition, one academic building, Tower 3, and one Cultural and Language Center (CLC), have also been constructed. PHO#1 was done in October 2025, with a 365-day maintenance period until October 2026. Currently, the status for the procurement of 10 Equipment and Furniture packages is 2 packages contracted (including the Furniture package consisting of 8 sub-packages), 4 packages in the contract preparation stage (planned for Q2/2026), 1 package in the bid evaluation stage, and 3 packages in tender preparation planned to be contracted in Q3/2026.
Data Source: MOECRT annual progress reports and ITS annual monitoring reports

Output: Indicator Indicator: UNILA upgraded with a new integrated research center with five laboratories in (i) tropical medicine; (ii) biomolecular, genetic, and degenerative diseases; (iii) pathology and toxicology; (iv) nutrition; and (v) clinical trial and diagnostic trial (with gender-responsive, earthquake-resilient, and climate-smart features) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Ongoing The upgrade of the integrated research center is included in the CWU package, namely the Integrated Research Center (IRC) Building. Laboratories, a meeting room, and a conference room are part of the five-floor building. The facility also offers communal space for students, which functions as a supporting system.
Data Source: MOECRT annual progress reports and UNILA annual monitoring reports

Output: Indicator Indicator: 75 ITS-industry partnerships on skills development and research and innovation in specialized areas established Achievement: 123 Progress/Status: Achieved Per September 2025, the number of industrial partnerships for the specialized areas of HETI is 123 partnerships.
Data Source: MOECRT annual progress reports and ITS annual monitoring reports

Output: Indicator Indicator: 20 UNILA-industry partnerships in skills development, research, and innovation in disciplines supported by the integrated research center established Achievement: 109 Progress/Status: Achieved Cumulatively, by the end of September 2025, UNILA had developed 109 partnerships in skills development, research, and innovation across various disciplines, derived from research activities, comparative studies, visiting professorships, training, and resource persons at international conferences organized by the UNILA HETI Project from 2022 to 2025, consisting of: - 10 MoU (between universities) - 14 MoA (between faculties and institutes) - 5 IA (between faculties or institutes) - 80 individual partnerships from research, comparative studies, fellowship programs, technical assistance, and the Professorship Program.
Data Source: MOECRT annual progress reports and UNILA annual monitoring reports
